summary: Sarah Wells Brooks was an Indologist. She studied at Radcliffe College in 1892 under Charles Rockwell Lanman.
Saraju Rath is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. She held posts at the International Institute for Asian Studies, attested in 2012 and 2022.

Sarasi Kumar Saraswati (1906–1983) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Sivaprasad Bhattacharyya and Jitendra Nath Banerjea, served as Librarian at The Asiatic Society in 1943, and held a post at the University of Calcutta.

Sarat Chandra Das (1849–1917) was a Tibetologist, Indologist, and linguist. Educated at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, and Presidency College, Chennai, he studied under Ugyen Gyatso and Sengchen Lobzang Palden Chöpel. He directed Bhutia Boarding School and served the Bengal government.

Sarat Sarma is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Manipur University (attested 2006) under the doctoral supervision of S. Shyamkishore Singh, having also studied under S. Lokendrajit Singh.

Sarath Piyananda Weerasekara works in Buddhist and religious studies. He pursued a PhD in Sinhala Medium at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under the supervision of Deshapriya Gunasena (attested 2026).

Saroj Kanta Kar works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Utkal University, GITAM University, M.S. University of Baroda, Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (2018–2021), and the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (2021–2022), returning to Utkal as Associate Professor in 2022.

Saroja Bhate is an Indologist and linguist. She served as Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 2000–2011) and as Honorary Secretary at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 2003).

Sarva Daman Singh worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and held posts at the University of Queensland, serving as Professor of History (attested 1958, 1987).

Sarvepalli Gopal (1923–2002) was a historian. He studied at Mill Hill School, Madras Christian College, Presidency College, Chennai, University of Madras, and Balliol College, Oxford (~1945–1951), and later held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1971–1983).

Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (1888–1975) was a philosopher and Indologist educated at Madras Christian College. His major posts included professorships at Mysore, Calcutta, and Oxford, Vice-Chancellorships at Andhra and Banaras Hindu University, and the Chancellorship of the University of Delhi.

Saswati Mutsuddy is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her MA, MPhil, and PhD at the University of Calcutta under Dipak Kumar Barua, and held a post in its Department of Pali in 2001.

Sati Shankar Dutta Pandey specializes in Indology and philosophy. He earned his master's and PhD at Banaras Hindu University (1981–1990) and became the Founder & Chief Functionary of the Global Synergetic Foundation in 1992.

Satiranjan Sen worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University, served as a Research Scholar and Junior Research Fellow at Visva-Bharati University, and founded Cheen Bharat Sanskriti.

Satish Chandra (1922–2017) was a historian and Indologist. He studied at the University of Allahabad (~1940–1948) and held posts at Aligarh Muslim University (~1953–1961) and the University of Rajasthan (~1963–1970).
Satish Chandra Garkoti is an Indologist who earned his PhD at Kumaun University (1988–1992). He held a post as Concurrent Faculty at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2008.

Satish Chandra Vidyabhusan (1870–1920) was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Krishnagar Government College, Sanskrit College, and University of Calcutta under Sarat Chandra Das, he served as Principal of Sanskrit College and held posts at The Asiatic Society.

Satish Kumar Tiwari is an Indologist and philosopher who earned his PhD from the University of Lucknow (2011–2017). He held Assistant Professor posts at Lucknow, Ganesh Dutt College, SMVD University, Mahendra Mahila College, and A.P.B. Government Post Graduate College.

Satkari Mookerjee (1896–1968) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He served as Ashutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (~1948–1955) and became Director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1955.
Satkari Mukhopadhyaya is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as Coordinator of the Kala Kosa Division at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (attested 1999, 2026).
